chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿĪsā al-Farrāʾ, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir عليه السلام said: “Whoever’s outward aspect is weightier than his inward self, his scale will be light.”
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:
"Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'When one among My creation who knows Me disobeys Me, I set over him, from My creation, one who does not know Me.'"

key_terms.بَاطِنِهِ: one’s inward reality or hidden inner self
key_terms.سَلَّطْتُ عَلَيْهِ: I set over him or gave authority over him
key_terms.ظَاهِرُهُ: one’s outward appearance or public state
key_terms.مِيزَانُهُ: his scale, meaning the scale of deeds in reckoning

ai.seo_question: What do these hadith say about hypocrisy, inward sincerity, and the consequences of knowingly disobeying Allah?
ai.summary: These reports warn against inner corruption hidden behind outward appearance and against knowingly disobeying Allah. The first ties true worth to inward sincerity rather than public display, while the second presents disobedience as a cause of humiliation and subjugation.
